title: Operational Restoration Prioritization Canvas
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

This document defines the Operational Restoration Prioritization Canvas (ORPC): a lightweight, repeatable framework platform operators and incident commanders use to triage, prioritize, and execute restoration actions during multi-service or tenant-impact incidents. The ORPC focuses on measurable customer impact, cost-to-recover, and long-term reliability trade-offs specific to Redwood Inference (serving runtime, routing, batching, and cache subsystems).

Goals

- Provide a consistent decision process for cross-team incidents (eng-platform, eng-serving-runtime, eng-sre, customer-success).
- Surface the minimal set of actions to restore acceptable SLOs while limiting cost/regression risk.
- Capture owner, timeline, and rollback criteria for each prioritized action.

When to use this canvas

Use the ORPC for incidents where:
1) >1 subsystem or service is impaired (examples: batch scheduler + KV prefix cache; routing + model variant availability), OR
2) Multiple customers/tenants report varied symptom severity, OR
3) There is uncertainty which mitigation yields fastest restoration without causing cascading failure.

High-level process (1-page flow)

1. Initial assessment (5–10 minutes): scope, active SLOs, top-affected tenants.
2. Populate ORPC scoring table (10 minutes): impact, exposure, cost-to-recover, rollback difficulty.
3. Rank candidate mitigations.
4. Assign owners and run parallel actions where safe.
5. Validate metrics and iterate; if no improvement in 10–15 minutes, escalate to fallback plan.

Key definitions and scoring guidance

- Customer Impact (0–5): severity of visible user-facing failures. 0 = no impact; 5 = complete outage for paying tenants.
- SLO Deviation (0–5): how far measured SLOs are beyond target (e.g., 99th latency breach, error rate).
- Breadth (0–5): number of tenants/features affected (0 = single internal test, 5 = all production traffic).
- Recovery Effort (0–5): expected engineering time + coordination (0 = <5 minutes, 5 = requires cross-region deploys or infra changes).
- Regression Risk (0–5): chance the mitigation introduces new production regressions (0 = negligible, 5 = high).
- Cost Delta (0–5): incremental cloud/GPU cost of the mitigation (0 = free, 5 = sustained high-cost burst).

Scoring matrix (example table)

| Candidate Mitigation | Customer Impact | SLO Deviation | Breadth | Recovery Effort | Regression Risk | Cost Delta | Weighted Score |
|----------------------|-----------------|---------------|---------|-----------------|-----------------|------------|----------------|
| Route to model-2 (quantized) | 4 | 3 | 3 | 1 | 2 | 1 | 14 |
| Disable batching for 95th perc. | 2 | 2 | 4 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 10 |
| Increase dedicated burst pool | 5 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 5 | 26 |
| Fallback to hosted API | 3 | 2 | 4 | 2 | 1 | 3 | 15 |

Weighting recommendations (default weights)

- Customer Impact: x3
- SLO Deviation: x2
- Breadth: x1
- Recovery Effort: x1
- Regression Risk: x1
- Cost Delta: x0.5

(Score = sum(weighted component scores) — teams may adjust weights for specific incidents; document chosen weights in post-incident notes.)

Template: ORPC card (copy into incident page)

- Incident ID: 
- Time started: 
- Lead IC: 
- Affected services: (list service names: e.g., runtime-batcher, kv-prefix-cache, router-ingress)
- Primary SLOs impacted: (e.g., gen-99-latency, embed-p99, error-rate)
- Top 3 affected tenants: 

Candidate Mitigations (one row per action):

- Title:
- Short description:
- Expected effect (metrics to watch):
- Score (numeric):
- Owner:
- Runbook steps (numbered):
- Verification checks (dashboard panels / queries):
- Rollback criteria:

Example candidate mitigations and tested runbooks

1) Route-to-quantized-variant (fast path)
- Short description: divert % of traffic to a compatible quantized variant of the model for affected tenants.
- Expected effect: reduce GPU mem pressure and kernel stalls; improves tail latency.
- Runbook steps:
  1. Update routing policy via route-service CLI: rw-route update --policy tenant-priority --model-id MODEL-2-QUANT --percent 20
  2. Monitor gen-99-latency (per-tenant) and model-error-rate for 10 minutes.
  3. Gradually increase percent if latency improves and model error < 0.5%.
- Verification: dashboard panels 'models.per_tenant.latency.99', 'model-variant.error-rate'
- Rollback: route back to original variant if model error rises above 0.5% or token quality regression flagged by eval guardrail.

2) Batching safe-mode (local change, fast rollback)
- Short description: temporarily reduce max batch size and disable speculative batching for latency-sensitive routes.
- Runbook steps:
  1. Apply feature toggle: ff toggle batch-safe-mode --routes=route-ids --value=on
  2. Adjust scheduler target_x_latency_ms to 25ms via scheduler API.
  3. Observe per-route latency and throughput for 5 minutes.
- Verification: panels 'batcher.avg_batch_size', 'route.latency.p95/p99'
- Rollback: flip toggle off if throughput drops >30% without latency gain.

3) Emergency capacity add (high cost)
- Short description: provision Dedicated burst capacity in region-us-west-2 for 60 minutes.
- Runbook steps:
  1. Request burst via capacity service: capacity request --pool dedicated-usw2-burst --gpus 8 --duration 60m --reason "Incident <ID>"
  2. Confirm nodes join pool and autoscaler updates target.
  3. Re-route traffic according to policy 'burst-first' for highest-priority tenants.
- Verification: 'gpu-pool.utilization', 'route.success-rate'
- Rollback: drain burst nodes and deprovision after stabilization; provide cost note to finance.

Operational safety checks (must be completed before mitigation)

- Ownership declared (owner + backup).
- Dashboard panel(s) identified and pinned to incident page.
- Clear rollback criterion written and agreed by owner.
- If mitigation touches model variants or quantized binaries: run smoke-eval with a representative prompt set (<= 30 samples) before wide rollout.

Common mistakes and how to avoid them

- Mistake: Prioritizing cost-saving mitigations that prolong user-visible degradation. Fix: enforce minimum restoration threshold (reduce customer impact to <=2) as a requirement for all cost-aware actions.
- Mistake: Applying aggressive routing changes without assessing model output quality. Fix: use smoke-eval and monitor quality metrics (BLEU-like score or eval-guardrail signals) during rollout.

Post-incident requirements

- Populate final ORPC card in the incident retrospective with: chosen weights, final scores, timeline of actions, tangible metrics improvement, cost delta estimate, and follow-up tasks.
- If mitigation introduced a regression, open a P1 bug and link to incident.
- Owner of retrospective: lead IC; slides due within 3 business days.

Quick reference commands and config snippets

- Route update (example):
  rw-route update --service router-ingress --policy "percent: {MODEL-2-QUANT: 30, MODEL-3: 70}" --reason "ORPC: route-to-quantized-variant"

- Feature flag toggle (example YAML snippet for deployments):
  featureFlags:
    batch-safe-mode:
      enabled: true
      routes: ["/v1/generate", "/v1/chat"]
      initiatedBy: "incident/opercanvas"

- Scheduler API example (curl):
  curl -X POST https://scheduler.internal/api/v1/update -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"target_x_latency_ms":25}'

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owners: eng-platform oncall + runtime team lead.
- Escalation path: if no metric improvement after 15 minutes, escalate to eng-sre channel and notify platform director.
- Finance notification: any Emergency capacity add must be cc:ed to finance-alerts@redwood.com with estimated cost.

Appendix: Example incident summary (filled)

- Incident ID: RWI-INC-2026-043
- Time started: 2026-01-17T09:12Z
- Lead IC: Maya Chen
- Affected services: runtime-batcher, kv-prefix-cache, router-ingress
- Primary SLOs impacted: gen-99-latency (target 800ms, observed 2200ms), embed-p99 (target 150ms, observed 420ms)
- Top mitigation chosen: route-to-quantized-variant (MODEL-2-QUANT) -> score 18
- Outcome: gen-99-latency reduced to 720ms within 12 minutes; minor quality regression detected for 2 tenants and rolled back; follow-ups: automated smoke-eval on route-change (owner: runtime)

Contact and related resources

- Incident runbook template: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/incident-runbook-template
- Routing service docs: /confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/router-ingress-design
- Cost attribution dashboard: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/token-cost-attribution-and-explainable-trace-playbook-2026

Notes

This canvas is intentionally concise so it can be completed in-parallel with short-lived actions. Teams are encouraged to adapt scoring weights and add custom checks for industry customers with stricter compliance needs. Update the ORPC template in this page when operational primitives (routing CLI, scheduler API) change.
